rationale: A network service rejects the requester's credentials; the gateway is reachable, so this is a credential rejection rather than connectivity loss.
The only required field is empty, so no symptom can be read.

state.ticket_text: Since Monday the softphone calls from my desk have been choppy and intranet pages take a long time to load. Separately, this morning my laptop can see the office wireless network in the list but will not stay joined; it drops every few minutes and I have to rejoin. My password was accepted every time it reconnected, so it is not a login problem.

rationale: The text reports two symptoms, latency_or_packet_loss and wireless_association, and the contract's precedence order places wireless_association ahead of latency_or_packet_loss. The remark that the password was accepted negates a credential rejection rather than describing one, so authentication_or_access does not apply.

state.maintenance_notice: Firmware upgrade on the Riverside edge router pair, Saturday 01:00 to 03:00 local time. The routers will be upgraded one at a time and the procedure is expected to be hitless; no user-visible interruption is expected for Riverside staff or for internet access. Note that the site-to-site tunnel to Harbor Point will drop for roughly two minutes during each failover, so Harbor Point users will briefly lose access to applications hosted at Riverside.

rationale: The notice states no impact for Riverside users but an expected two-minute interruption for Harbor Point users and says what they will experience. The contract says a notice that states an interruption for some scope and no impact for other scopes is affected_scope_stated, so the prominent no-impact language does not yield no_impact_expected.

state.alert_policy: 1. Any alert reporting an interface or link going down or flapping requires acknowledgement by the on-call engineer within 15 minutes. 2. Link flap alerts from lab access switches, regardless of transition count, are recorded only and clear on their own; no action is taken. 3.
